FULL DESIGN DOCUMENT (all 5 approved fixes incorporated).

§0 COMPONENT IDENTIFICATION (verify before execution): No InfLLM paper/code in sandbox; mapping inferred from the Infini-attention/constant-memory-transformer family. "Dynamic context memory lookup" = query-keyed (content-driven) read over a constant-size compressed memory, mixed with recent-window softmax attention. "Unit representations" = the form in which each context element is stored in memory: granularity (per-token vs per-chunk) x learned vs non-learned compression; default presumed to be a learned per-token compressed vector. Flagged as inferred, must be verified against paper/code — shakiest point.

§1 OBJECTIVE: Decompose long-context performance into two levers; quantify each as a share of the long-context gain, reported per length. H_a: lookup dynamism matters; H_b: unit-representation choice matters.

§2 VARIABLES/CONDITIONS (fixes #2,#3): Lookup axis 3 levels — L0 dynamic (query-keyed read), L-rec recency-window, L-unif uniform-over-memory. Unit axis 3 levels — U0 default, U-alt1 chunk-level, U-alt2 non-learned mean-pool. Conditions: C0 (L0,U0) reference; L-rec (recency,U0); L-unif (uniform,U0); U-alt1 (L0,chunk); U-alt2 (L0,mean-pool); INT (recency,chunk); CEIL; FLOOR. Lookup claim requires L0 to beat BOTH non-dynamic variants; both are run and reported. Because memory is constant-size, L-unif is O(memory) and feasible at 256k; caveat: if memory is NOT constant-size, L-rec is the safe 256k variant and L-unif is limited to 128k. Two unit alternatives test whether the CHOICE matters (range across U0/U-alt1/U-alt2), not just one swap.

§3 TASKS (unchanged): RULER/needle-in-a-haystack + multi-needle (lookup probe); QuALITY/LooGLE long-doc QA (integration); QMSum/arXiv summarization (representation/aggregation).

§4 BASELINES/ANCHORS (fix #1): FLOOR = no-memory/short-ctx. CEIL per-length: true full-attention only where it fits (<=32k) — ratio valid only there. At 128k/256k full attention does not fit, so report (i) absolute delta in points as primary, plus (ii) a feasible per-length oracle = full attention over last 32k window, explicitly labeled a LOWER-BOUND ceiling, not the true one. Rule: never normalize by a nonexistent ceiling.

§5 CONTROLS (unchanged): lookup ablations use identical weights, only read path altered (exact param match); unit ablations report param delta (U-alt2 removes learned compression -> fewer params), add param-matched control if nontrivial; one factor per ablation; 3 seeds; constant memory size held fixed.

§6 ANALYSIS (fix #1): metric = accuracy/F1 over {4k,16k,32k,128k,256k} per condition/seed. Criticality score = (Perf_full - Perf_ablated)/(Perf_CEIL - Perf_FLOOR) only where true ceiling exists (<=32k); at long lengths report absolute points + recency-oracle value labeled lower-bound. Threshold unchanged: critical if >=20% of gain lost AND paired-bootstrap CI significant; non-critical if CI overlaps 0 / loss <~5%. Report per length. Lookup verdict: dynamism critical iff L0 > {L-rec,L-unif} significantly by >=20% of gain. Unit verdict: choice critical iff spread across {U0,U-alt1,U-alt2} exceeds threshold and U0 not interchangeable.

§7 FEASIBILITY/BUDGET (fix #5): Primary = inference-time intervention on a frozen InfLLM checkpoint, ONE A100/H100-class 80GB GPU, no retraining. Matrix = 8 conditions x 5 lengths x 3 task suites x 3 seeds, ~40 prompts/cell => ~14,400 prompt-runs. Wall time ~15 s/prompt (prefill-dominated; 10-60s at 128k/256k, 1-5s short). Per condition ~7.5 GPU-hrs; full matrix ~60 GPU-hrs ~ 2.5-3 days single GPU (batching at short lengths reduces). Core reduced config = 3 lengths x ~25 prompts/cell ~ 20 GPU-hrs ~ 1 day. Memory check: 7B fp16 + constant memory + 256k activations fit 80GB with chunked prefill/KV offload; if memory not constant-size, 256k may need offload/smaller batch — benchmark 256k prefill first. Retraining fallback = one-paragraph contingency only (multi-GPU, days-weeks per variant, shrink to one ablation per factor), not a parallel plan.

§8 LIMITATIONS: frozen-model co-adaptation means inference-time ablation is an UPPER BOUND on criticality; ceiling validity <=32k only; single base model size; inferred component mapping gates everything; sampling variance/task coverage with 3 seeds and 3 suites.

§9 WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE DESIGN: exact InfLLM component definitions + whether memory is constant-size; access (code+weights vs black-box API -> reimplementation fallback); true model size/context range and compute beyond one 80GB GPU.

# Experiment Design: Criticality of Dynamic Context-Memory Lookup and Unit-Representation Choice in InfLLM

**Deliverable type:** design only. Nothing is executed; feasibility = "could a reasonable team do this with the stated resources."

## 0. Component identification (verify before execution)

There is **no InfLLM paper or code in the sandbox**, so the following mapping is **inferred from the Infini-attention / constant-memory-transformer family** and **must be verified against the paper or source before any run.**

- **"Dynamic context memory lookup"** — working definition: InfLLM keeps a **constant-size compressed memory** of past context (written via a linear-attention-style update) and, at each step, produces attention as a mix of (i) softmax attention over a recent window and (ii) a **read term keyed by the current query** over that memory. "Dynamic" = the read is **content-driven** (the query selects which past information is retrieved), not a fixed/positional access. The ablation targets this *query-keyed read path*.
- **"Unit representations"** — working definition: the form in which each element of context is **stored in the memory** — a *unit*. Dimensions of choice: **granularity** (per-token vs. per-chunk pooled vector) and **learned vs. non-learned compression** (a learned projection vs. plain mean-pool). Given Infini-attention's per-token learned write, the **default is presumed to be a learned per-token compressed vector**; the two alternatives are defined relative to that (see §2).

> **Status:** these are my best mapping, not sourced facts. If the real InfLLM defines these components differently (e.g., memory is not constant-size, or "unit" means something else), §2's ablation forms change. This is the shakiest point in the whole design.

## 1. Objective and hypothesis

Decompose InfLLM's long-context performance into two levers and quantify each as a *share of the long-context gain*:
- **H_a:** the *dynamism* of the memory lookup (vs. any non-dynamic access) is responsible for a large share of long-context performance.
- **H_b:** the *specific choice* of unit representation (vs. other reasonable representations) is responsible for a large share.

A factor is "critical" only if removing/changing it loses a meaningful, statistically significant share of the gain — and we report this **per context length**, because criticality is expected to be length-dependent.

## 2. Variables and conditions

**Lookup axis (3 levels):**
- **L0 — dynamic:** the real query-keyed read (reference).
- **L-rec — recency-window (non-dynamic):** replace the query-keyed read with attention restricted to the recent window only (bounded, O(window)).
- **L-unif — uniform-over-memory (non-dynamic):** keep the memory but read it with a **query-independent uniform weight** (no content-driven selection).

**Unit axis (3 levels):**
- **U0 — default:** InfLLM's native unit representation.
- **U-alt1 — chunk-level:** pool *k* tokens into one memory unit (coarser granularity, same learned compression where applicable).
- **U-alt2 — non-learned mean-pool:** drop the learned compression; store a plain mean-pooled vector per unit.

**Conditions (one-factor-at-a-time from a center, plus one interaction cell):**

| ID | Lookup | Units | Purpose |
|----|--------|-------|---------|
| C0 | L0 dynamic | U0 | reference (full InfLLM) |
| L-rec | recency | U0 | lookup ablation — recency |
| L-unif | uniform | U0 | lookup ablation — uniform |
| U-alt1 | L0 dynamic | chunk-level | unit ablation 1 |
| U-alt2 | L0 dynamic | mean-pool | unit ablation 2 |
| INT | recency | chunk-level | interaction (do the two compound?) |
| CEIL | full attention | n/a | ceiling (per-length, §4) |
| FLOOR | no memory / short ctx | n/a | floor |

**On the lookup claim (fix #2):** dynamism "matters" only if **L0 beats *both* L-rec and L-unif.** We run and report both. **Feasibility at 256k:** because the memory is *constant-size*, uniform-over-memory is O(memory_size) and cheap at any length, so **both variants are feasible at 256k** *provided* the memory is truly constant-size. **Caveat:** if component-identification reveals the memory is *not* constant-size (scales with stored units), then L-unif grows with context and **L-rec is the safe 256k variant** — we would then run L-unif only to 128k and say so.

**On the unit claim (fix #3):** with **two** alternatives, "the choice matters" is tested as a *range*: the spread across {U0, U-alt1, U-alt2} tells us whether the default sits at an optimum or whether any reasonable representation performs comparably. One swap could not distinguish "this alternative is just bad" from "the choice is critical."

## 3. Tasks and benchmarks (kept as agreed)

- **RULER / needle-in-a-haystack (incl. multi-needle):** pure retrieval across positions/lengths — the clean probe for the **lookup** lever.
- **Long-doc QA (QuALITY / LooGLE):** retrieval + reasoning — does the unit carry enough signal for *integration*?
- **Long summarization (QMSum / arXiv):** aggregation over the whole context — stresses the **unit representation** lever (does the compressed unit preserve enough to summarize faithfully?).

Retrieval-heavy tasks load the lookup lever; integration/aggregation tasks load the representation lever, so the two factors are exercised by different tasks.

## 4. Baselines and anchors (fix #1 — ceiling validity)

- **FLOOR:** no-memory / short-context baseline — the level we're trying to beat.
- **CEIL (per-length, stated explicitly):**
  - **≤ 32k:** true full-attention oracle over the whole context (it fits in memory). The ratio in §6 is **only valid here.**
  - **128k / 256k:** full attention over the entire context **does not fit in memory, so it is not a real ceiling.** Two options, used together:
    1. A **feasible per-length oracle** = full attention over the **last 32k window** (a "recency oracle"). We state clearly this is a **lower-bound ceiling, not the true one** — the true ceiling is unattainable at that length.
    2. **Report the absolute delta in points** (Perf_full − Perf_ablated) alongside, so no number is normalized by a nonexistent ceiling.

**Rule:** we never divide by a ceiling that does not exist. Ratio is reported only where the true oracle runs (≤32k); at longer lengths we report absolute points plus the recency-oracle-normalized value *labeled as a lower-bound ceiling*.

## 5. Controls

- **Matched parameters and compute:** lookup ablations (L-rec, L-unif) use **identical weights** and alter only the forward-pass read path → exact param match, near-identical FLOPs. Unit ablations: U-alt1 is same-or-fewer params; U-alt2 (mean-pool) **removes the learned compression** and has fewer params — we **report the param delta** per condition and, if nontrivial, add a param-matched control or flag it as a confound.
- **One factor changed per ablation** from the C0 center.
- **Multiple seeds** (3) to capture sampling variance.
- **Constant memory size** held fixed across lookup conditions so capacity doesn't confound the comparison.

## 6. Analysis plan, metric, threshold

- **Metric:** task accuracy/F1, swept over context length **{4k, 16k, 32k, 128k, 256k}**, per condition and seed.
- **Criticality score (where a true ceiling exists, ≤32k):**
  `score = (Perf_full − Perf_ablated) / (Perf_CEIL − Perf_FLOOR)` = share of the long-context gain the factor explains.
- **At 128k/256k:** report **absolute delta (points)** as primary, plus the recency-oracle-normalized value clearly labeled as a lower-bound ceiling.
- **Threshold (unchanged):** "critical" if ablating loses **≥ 20%** of the long-context gain **and** the gap is statistically significant via **paired bootstrap CI** (resampling over prompts/tasks/lengths, pooled across seeds); "non-critical" if the CI overlaps zero / loss **< ~5%**.
- **Report per length** — a factor can be critical at 256k and irrelevant at 8k; a single pooled number would hide that.
- **Lookup verdict:** dynamism is critical iff L0 > {L-rec, L-unif} by a significant, ≥20%-of-gain margin. **Unit verdict:** the choice is critical iff the spread across {U0, U-alt1, U-alt2} exceeds the significance threshold and U0 is not statistically interchangeable with the alternatives.

## 7. Feasibility and budget (fix #5)

**Primary path: inference-time intervention on a frozen InfLLM checkpoint** (disable/alter the read path; swap the memory write) — **one A100/H100-class (80 GB) GPU.** No retraining.

- Prompts per (suite, length) cell ≈ 40 (RULER needle ~50, RULER multi-needle ~50, QuALITY ~30, QMSum ~20; ~40 avg).

- **Full matrix ≈ ~60 GPU-hours** ≈ **~2.5–3 days** on a single 80 GB GPU (serial); modest batching at short lengths reduces this.
